title: FRust worksheet scalar API
keywords: frust worksheet scalar variables calculation engineering math_set_scalar math_get_scalar
text: Worksheet FRust cells and the full editor share the actual scalar workspace. Define pub fn run() -> String = { ... }. math_set_scalar(name: String, value: f64) -> i64 stores a finite scalar (1 success, 0 invalid); math_get_scalar(name: String) -> f64 reads it (NaN when missing). Names use letters, digits, underscores. print_line(text: String) records output. Run a cell, then inspect actual execution_status and workspace_inspect. No symbolic or matrix solver backend is implemented in the foundation.

title: Implemented foundation and mathematical roadmap
keywords: symbolic matrix solvers numerical units plotting capabilities implemented equations typeset
text: Implemented: worksheets with notes, FRust calculation cells and typeset mathematics cells (structured equations entered in linear notation, rendered natively, saved as structured trees), native FRust JIT, finite-real scalar workspace, FRust syntax checking, the node programming editor with compiler and debugger, the audio pipeline, DSP effects compiled to native code with live audition and offline rendering, VST3 export (shared plugin identity), layouts, account integration, DPAPI BYOK storage, filesystem LiteSemRAG reference cards and agent tools. Math cells are not evaluated yet: there is no mathematical compiler, symbolic algebra, matrix or unit support, plotting, or direct mouse editing of equations. Planned: those, and the Math-to-FRust compiler. Do not claim planned mathematical functions work yet.

title: Engineering units in this first milestone
keywords: units dimensions metres meters millimetres current voltage resistance physics
text: Automatic dimensional quantities are planned. For current scalar computations document unit conventions explicitly in worksheet notes and variable names, and report them with results. Do not silently reinterpret radians as degrees or m as mm. MathSession stores finite IEEE double values only.

title: FRust syntax that works in Djehuti Math
keywords: frust syntax language let mut while if function array string print_line errors syntax error program
text: A script defines pub fn run() -> String = { ... }. Statements end with ;. The last expression (no ;) is the value. let x: f64 = 1.0; let mut n: i64 = 0; n = n + 1; i as f64 casts. while n < 10 { ... }; and if (cond) { ... }; blocks are followed by a semicolon. Numbers have no exponent notation (write 0.000001, not 1e-6); write 0.0 - x for negation. Types: i64, f64, bool, String. Comments start with //. print_line(text: String) records output. There are NO sqrt, sin, cos or similar functions in ordinary scripts; the only math host functions are math_set_scalar and math_get_scalar. DSP effects may declare extern fn djehuti_dsp_sin etc. (see math.dsp.effect-contract). Use frust_check to see line:column diagnostics before running.

title: DSP effect contract and directives
keywords: dsp effect audio process_sample directives param workspace coeffs sample rate vst contract filter distortion
text: An effect is FRust defining pub fn process_sample(audio_in: f64, ws: Array<f64, W>, coeffs: Array<f64, P+1>) -> f64, called per sample and channel. ws is the persistent state of that channel (W entries, zero at start; assign ws[0] = value;). coeffs[0..P) are the declared parameters in order and coeffs[P] is the sample rate. Comment directives declare it: // @effect Name, // @id com.example.name, // @param id "Label" min max default [unit], // @workspace W. The signature array sizes must match (W and P+1). Parameter ids bypass, input_gain_db, output_level_db and mix are reserved. Host math functions you may call (declared for you): djehuti_dsp_exp, _log, _sin, _cos, _tan, _tanh, _atan, _sqrt, _pow(x, y). Flow: dsp_template or dsp_source, dsp_compile, dsp_render (measure), dsp_live, vst_export. A Math-to-FRust compiler will later produce the same contract.

title: Node programming workflow
keywords: node program graph designer compile debug workflow pins connect literal state machine
text: Use node_program_new, then node_program_node_types to see types and pins, node_program_add_node, node_program_connect (output pin to input pin), node_program_set_parameter for literals, node_program_validate, node_program_compile to see the generated FRust, node_program_run to execute it, and node_debug_marker with node_debug_start / node_debug_control / node_debug_inspect to debug. Programs are saved as .frnode.json with node_program_save. Nodes compile to real FRust source; there is no separate node interpreter.

title: Audio pipeline and VST3 limits
keywords: audio device input output wav vst3 plugin identity limitation host latency
text: The audio pipeline opens the default devices only when asked (dsp_live, audio_status open=true, Audio Settings). Live processing is mono per callback and copied to all outputs. dsp_render is offline and needs no device. VST3 export copies the precompiled Djehuti Math Effect runtime and stores the compiled effect in Contents/Resources; every export therefore has the compiled VST3 class identity of the runtime, so a host cannot distinguish two different exports by class. Loading of an exported bundle was checked only with the in-app check, not in a commercial DAW.

title: Math cells and linear notation
keywords: math cell equation typeset notation fraction sqrt root superscript subscript sum integral greek placeholder role system
text: A math cell holds structured mathematics (fractions, roots, scripts, delimiters, large operators, placeholders) with stable node ids; the linear text is only how it was entered. Linear notation: write (x^2+1)/(x+3), sqrt(x^2+1), root(3, x), F=m*a, sum_(i=1)^n i^2, int_0^1 x dx, alpha, Omega, pi, infty, partial, <=, >=, !=, ->, :=. '/' divides the factors written just before it (a run with no operator between them, like 2x or f(x)) by the single factor after it; use parentheses to group, so a+b/c divides only b and (a+b)/c divides both. '^' and '_' attach to the factor before; x^(n+1) takes a group; a trailing apostrophe is a prime. Letters written together are one name (rate, dv); put a space or * between letters to multiply. Function names (sin, cos, ln, exp...) are upright. A missing operand becomes a placeholder (a dashed box), which is a valid, incomplete state. Roles: expression, definition, equation, constraint, assumption, system. A system has one equation per line and aligns on &. Use worksheet_add_cell kind math, then worksheet_math_snapshot to read the structure.
